blocks.value: **No base case.** `StackOverflowError`. Every recursive method needs at least one.

**A base case that is never reached.** Having one is not enough: each call must move toward it. `factorial(n - 1)` with a negative argument recurses forever past `num == 0`; guarding with `num <= 0` is safer.
**Forgetting to return the recursive call's result.**

if (num == 0) { return 1; }
factorial(num - 1);           // result computed, then thrown away
**Not reducing the problem.** `factorial(num)` instead of `factorial(num - 1)` calls itself with identical arguments forever.
**Recursing too deep.** Java's default stack handles only a few thousand frames. A recursion 100,000 levels deep overflows regardless of correctness, use iteration there.
**Recomputing the same values.** Naive recursive Fibonacci recalculates the same subproblems exponentially many times; `fib(50)` effectively never finishes.
**Putting work on the wrong side of the recursive call.** Before it, work happens on the way down; after it, on the way back up. Getting this backwards reverses your output.
